slides.heading: Design Fundamentals 2/4
slides.subtitle: Topics 7–12
slides.narration: Design fundamentals, part 2 of 4. We'll cover Caching, Proxies, Load balancers, Hashing, Relational databases, and Key-value stores.

slides.heading: 7. Caching
slides.narration: Caching. Client, server, CDN, DB caches. Write-through versus write-back. eviction policies LRU or LFU. staleness and invalidation.

slides.heading: 8. Proxies
bullets: Forward proxy (acts for the client) vs reverse proxy (acts for the server: LB, TLS termination, caching)
slides.narration: Proxies. Forward proxy (acts for the client) versus reverse proxy (acts for the server: LB, TLS termination, caching). Nginx.

slides.heading: 9. Load balancers
bullets: Round robin, weighted, least-connections, IP/consistent hashing
slides.narration: Load balancers. Round robin, weighted, least-connections, IP or consistent hashing. health checks. L4 versus L7.

slides.heading: 10. Hashing
bullets: Consistent hashing and rendezvous hashing keep remapping small when servers join or leave
slides.narration: Hashing. Consistent hashing and rendezvous hashing keep remapping small when servers join or leave.

slides.heading: 11. Relational databases
bullets: SQL, ACID transactions, indexes (B-trees), strong consistency, joins
slides.narration: Relational databases. SQL, ACID transactions, indexes (B-trees), strong consistency, joins.

slides.heading: 12. Key-value stores
slides.narration: Key-value stores. Simple get or put, very fast, flexible. Redis (memory), DynamoDB, etcd or ZooKeeper (strongly consistent config).

slides.heading: Recap
slides.narration: To recap this part: Caching; Proxies; Load balancers; Hashing; Relational databases; Key-value stores. Each of these shows up again in the design walkthroughs.
